oil.summary: Brent closed above $91 and WTI at $84.51, extending a powerful multi-week rally driven by the escalating US-Iran conflict and the effective chokehold on the Strait of Hormuz. A Kuwait-flagged products tanker was struck in the strait today, and Houthis forced two Saudi tankers to U-turn in the Red Sea, keeping the supply-risk premium firmly in play. An early morning pullback on ceasefire-negotiation reports was short-lived as the US-Iran MOU collapsed before the 30-day mark. Goldman Sachs warned crude could reach $120 if the strait remains disrupted into year-end. The crude-product divergence is notable: RBOB fell 5.07% on the day and heating oil dropped 2.89%, suggesting some demand-side concern despite tight crude supply. India continues buying Russian crude at near-record volumes despite the expiry of its US waiver.
drivers: Strait of Hormuz tanker strike and Houthi Red Sea attacks sustain acute supply-disruption premium on crude
US-Iran MOU collapse and proposed inclusion of Iran in Russia sanctions bill eliminates near-term diplomatic relief
Goldman $120/bbl price target and ceasefire-hope-driven intraday volatility highlight elevated geopolitical uncertainty

gas.summary: The US-Europe gas divergence widened sharply today. Henry Hub drifted fractionally lower to $2.856/MMBtu, continuing its month-long slide of nearly 12%, with no supportive domestic catalysts in today's headlines. European TTF surged 2.35% on the day to €58.74/MWh — up 40% over the past month — as the Strait of Hormuz closure strands Qatari LNG cargoes and forces spot-hungry buyers like Pakistan to pay record prices. ADNOC's $6.2bn FID on the Umm Shaif Gas Cap project in Abu Dhabi signals longer-dated supply development but offers no near-term relief to the disrupted LNG trade flows.
drivers: Hormuz closure stranding Qatari LNG cargoes drives TTF sharply higher and pushes Pakistan to record spot LNG prices
Henry Hub remains under pressure, down ~12% on the month, with no bullish domestic news flow today
ADNOC's $6.2bn Umm Shaif Gas Cap FID adds long-term supply but provides no short-term market relief

power.summary: The power and carbon complex presents a mixed picture dominated by geopolitical noise. EU carbon (EUA) was nearly unchanged at $78.59, with the one-month gain a modest 2%, lagging the surge in TTF gas which acts as a key input cost for European power generation. Iran warned of nuclear safety risks following a US strike on an unfinished Iranian nuclear plant, adding a new dimension to the conflict. Ukraine continued drone strikes on Russian energy and military targets. On the policy side, newly installed UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham announced the scrapping of the 5% VAT on electricity, a notable consumer-relief measure. Data for this sector is relatively thin today beyond these headline items.
drivers: US strike on Iran's unfinished nuclear plant raises safety concerns and broadens the geopolitical risk landscape
UK scraps 5% VAT on electricity under new PM Andy Burnham, reducing consumer power costs
TTF gas up 40% month-on-month pressures European power generation costs, yet EUA prices remain subdued, up only ~2% on the month
